title: tdx-guest: Expose the native attestation service API
overview: This patch refactors the TDX guest driver so that TDREPORT, Quote and RTMR operations are available as an in-kernel service (struct tdx_guest_ops) in addition to the existing misc ioctl, TSM report and TSM MR frontends, all sharing the same locks and buffers. It adds a one-client register/unregister interface in include/linux/tdx-guest.h that the TDX attestation family (patch 20) uses to attach to the device.

files.purpose: User documentation for the TDX guest driver; gains a section describing the kernel-client interface.

units.title: Kernel clients section
units.summary: Explains the single in-kernel client, its lifetime tied to the misc device, and attach/detach ordering.
units.details: Registration attaches immediately if the service is ready, otherwise at the end of `tdx_guest_init()`; module exit and unregistration both call the client's remove callback before buffers are freed.

files.purpose: Maintainer database entry for the TDX subsystem.

units.title: Add TDX guest files to the entry
units.summary: Lists the guest documentation, driver directory and new public header as maintained files.

files.purpose: The TDX guest platform driver: misc ioctl, TSM report (Quote) and TSM MR frontends over TDG.MR.REPORT, RTMR extend and the Quote protocol. This patch factors the core operations into lock-asserting helpers and layers the native client service over them.

units.title: Include tdx-guest.h
units.summary: Pulls in the new public service header.

units.title: Service state and length assertions
units.summary: Adds the construction-info store, a forward declaration of the misc device, and compile-time checks that public and driver lengths agree.

units.title: Client registration state
units.summary: client_lock protects the registered client, its private data and the tdx_service_ready flag.
units.details: `tdx_service_ready` is set at the end of init and cleared at exit; a client is attached only when both a client and readiness exist.

units.title: __tdx_do_report() and tdx_do_report()
units.summary: Splits the TDREPORT call into a locked worker and an interruptible-lock wrapper.
units.details: `__tdx_do_report()` asserts `mr_lock` is held, optionally copies in report data, issues `tdx_mcall_get_report0()`, and optionally copies the report out. `tdx_do_report()` keeps its old signature for the ioctl and TSM paths by taking `mr_lock` with `scoped_cond_guard(mutex_intr)`. Native callers use the worker directly with kernel sockptrs.

units.title: Device validation and info/report ops
units.summary: tdx_guest_device_valid() checks the device handle; info_get returns the cached info; report_get returns a fresh TDREPORT for the given report data.
units.details: Every native op returns -ENODEV unless `dev` is `tdx_misc_dev.this_device`. `tdx_guest_report_get()` checks the report-data length and output capacity, then under `mr_lock` runs `__tdx_do_report()` and copies `tdx_report_buf` out.

units.title: tdx_guest_mr_read()
units.summary: Reads MRTD or an RTMR by taking a fresh TDREPORT and copying the SHA-384 value at the register's report offset.
units.details: The static offsets table maps `enum tdx_guest_mr` to the TDREPORT_* field offsets; the report is generated under `mr_lock` so the value is consistent with concurrent extends.

units.title: tdx_guest_rtmr_extend()
units.summary: Validates the device and RTMR index (0-3) and delegates to the existing tdx_do_extend().

units.title: Capture construction fields in tdx_mr_init()
units.summary: After the initial report refresh, copies MRCONFIGID, MROWNER and MROWNERCONFIG into tdx_guest_info.
units.details: These fields are immutable after TD construction, so `info_get` can serve them without issuing a TDCALL.

units.title: Quote length assertion
units.summary: Ties the public Quote maximum to the driver's TDX_QUOTE_MAX_LEN.

units.title: __tdx_guest_quote_get() - signature and preconditions
units.summary: Converted from tdx_report_new_locked(): now a generic Quote worker taking report data and an output buffer, requiring quote_lock.
units.details: Argument validation (report-data length, non-NULL outputs) moved here from the TSM-specific code so that both TSM and native callers share it.

units.title: __tdx_guest_quote_get() - report data source
units.summary: The TDREPORT for the Quote is now generated from the caller-supplied report data pointer.

units.title: __tdx_guest_quote_get() - copy out
units.summary: Copies the Quote into the caller's buffer, bounded by capacity, instead of allocating a duplicate.
units.details: The TSM caller allocates its own buffer; the native caller supplies one. `out_len` has already been checked against `TDX_QUOTE_MAX_LEN`.

units.title: tdx_guest_quote_get()
units.summary: Native Quote op: validates the device, takes quote_lock interruptibly, and calls __tdx_guest_quote_get().

units.title: tdx_report_new_locked() - TSM wrapper
units.summary: TSM report path rewritten as a thin wrapper that allocates a TDX_QUOTE_MAX_LEN buffer and calls the shared worker.
units.details: Called from `tdx_report_new()` with `quote_lock` held. On success `report->outblob` takes ownership of the kvmalloc'd buffer sized to the actual Quote length; on error it is freed.

units.title: tdx_guest_ops table
units.summary: Binds the native operations to the driver's implementations; this table is what the client receives in add().

units.title: Client attach and detach
units.summary: Internal helpers, under client_lock, that call client->add() with the misc device and client->remove() with the saved private data.
units.details: `attach` is a no-op unless a client is registered and the service is ready; it records `tdx_client_priv` and `tdx_client_attached` on success. `detach` is a no-op when nothing is attached and always clears both.

units.title: tdx_guest_client_register()
units.summary: Registers the single native client and attaches it immediately if the service is already ready.
units.details: Requires both `add` and `remove`; a second registration gets -EBUSY. If attach fails, the registration is rolled back. Exported in the TDX_GUEST namespace.

units.title: tdx_guest_client_unregister()
units.summary: Detaches (calling remove) and clears the registered client, warning if the descriptor does not match.

units.title: tdx_guest_init() - mark ready and attach
units.summary: After TSM registration, flags the service ready and attaches any client registered earlier; failure unwinds.
units.details: If attach fails `tdx_service_ready` is reset and init jumps to `unregister_tsm`.

units.title: tdx_guest_init() - new unwind label
units.summary: Error label that unregisters the TSM report provider before the existing free_quote cleanup.

units.title: tdx_guest_exit() - detach client first
units.summary: Removes the attached client and marks the service not ready before tearing down TSM, Quote buffer and misc device.
units.details: This ordering ensures the client's remove callback runs before the report and Quote buffers are freed, as documented.

files.purpose: New in-kernel header defining the native TDX guest service: constants, construction info, the ops table the driver provides, and the client add/remove contract. Included by tdx-guest.c and by the attestation TDX provider.

units.title: Constants, tdx_guest_info and tdx_guest_mr
units.summary: Length constants mirroring the UAPI/driver values, the immutable construction fields, and the readable MR identifiers.
units.details: tdx-guest.c static_asserts that `TDX_GUEST_REPORTDATA_LEN`, `TDX_GUEST_REPORT_LEN` and `TDX_GUEST_QUOTE_MAX_LEN` equal the driver's own constants. `tdx_guest_info` holds MRCONFIGID, MROWNER and MROWNERCONFIG, captured once at init.

units.title: struct tdx_guest_ops
units.summary: Operations table the driver gives to its client: info, TDREPORT, Quote, MR read and RTMR extend.
units.details: Each op takes the `struct device *` handed out in `add` as proof of lifetime; buffer-returning ops take an output pointer, a capacity and an out-length.

units.title: struct tdx_guest_client and registration API
units.summary: Client descriptor with add/remove callbacks and the register/unregister prototypes.
units.details: `add()` returns client private data or an ERR_PTR; `remove()` receives that data. Only one client can be registered at a time.
